summary: Renders polygon and curve edges as wireframe lines with configurable color, wireframe mode, line width, and common MAT render-state controls.

key_params.name: topologywireframe
key_params.note: Use topology wireframe mode when available

key_params.name: polygonoffset
key_params.note: Offset depth to reduce Z-fighting with filled geometry

key_concepts: Wireframe MAT renders polygon and curve edges as lines, making it a material for edge visualization rather than filled surface shading.
OpenGL Tessellated Wire Frame follows the GPU-rendered tessellation, while Topology Wire Frame follows the source SOP primitive topology.
Wire color, alpha, and line width define the visible wire result, while the input geometry determines which edges can be drawn.
Depth test, depth writing, cull face, and polygon offset control whether wires appear over, behind, or fighting with coplanar filled geometry.
Deform and common MAT render states still apply, so skinned or transparent wireframe materials need the same render-state review as shaded materials.
common_gotchas: Wireframe renders edges, not filled surfaces; pair with another material or pass when filled shading is also needed.
Depth test and polygon offset determine whether wires fight with coplanar shaded geometry.
Topology wireframe and OpenGL-tessellated wireframe modes can show different edge sets.
Line width is in pixels and may not scale like world-space geometry.
